# MedBox — operator's guide

**ESA Horizon · 40 crew · no doctor aboard, no contact with Earth.**

> **This is a research and education instrument. It is not a medical device and it does not diagnose.** It gives you an urgency ordering computed from a published clinical score, and an assistant that offers hypotheses with the reading behind each one. Every number on the screen can be traced back to the instrument that produced it.

## 1. The one thing to understand first

The box runs on two tracks, and they are not equally important.

The **fast track** reads the sensors, scores each crew member with NEWS2 and redraws the board. It has no AI in it anywhere. It cannot be slowed down, confused or talked out of a reading.

The **slow track** is the assistant. It suggests, it narrates, it listens. It is allowed to be slow and it is allowed to die.

You do not need to remember which of your tools belong to which track, because the guide on the screen marks them and so does this one. But when somebody asks you on Friday what happens if the AI fails, the answer is: the vitals keep updating, the ordering holds, quarantine still assigns berths, the session still records, and the assistant stops narrating. The station's own spoken alerts carry on, starting with one that says the assistant has stopped. That is all.

## 2. Starting the station

One command, one process, one port. The interface is served by the same program that reads the sensors, so there is no second thing to start and nothing to configure.

```
Linux / macOS    .venv/bin/python medbox.py
Windows          .\.venv\Scripts\python medbox.py
```

Then open <http://127.0.0.1:8080>.

If that is the first time on this machine, run the installer first (`./setup.sh`, or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File setup.ps1`). It is described in `README.md` and it is safe to run again at any time.

You get two views of the same station, live at the same time:

| Where | What it is | When to use it |
|---|---|---|
| `http://127.0.0.1:8080/` | The ship. A 3D deck plan, crew at their stations, bulkheads that close. | The demo. |
| `http://127.0.0.1:8080/board` | The flat board. Same data, no 3D. | A machine with no working WebGL, or a projector that hates you. |

Both read the same feed and update together: the readings, the ordering, quarantine and the assistant are the same on both. The flat one has no Help panel, no command box and no spoken alerts, so on a machine that can run the ship, present from the ship.

## 3. Reading the board

The crew are ordered by NEWS2 aggregate, worst at the top. The ordering is the product: you should never have to hunt for the person who needs you.

Each row carries the crew member, their four vitals, the aggregate, and the band that aggregate falls in.

| NEWS2 aggregate | Band | What the score means you do |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | **routine** | Routine monitoring, 12-hourly. |
| 1–4 | **low** | Ward-based review by a competent clinician. |
| 5–6 | **medium** | Urgent review. Escalate to the medical officer. |
| 7 or more | **high** | Emergency response. Continuous monitoring. |

**The rule people forget:** any single parameter scoring 3 on its own escalates to **medium**, whatever the aggregate says. One catastrophic reading in an otherwise calm set is exactly the patient a total would hide, so the box applies the rule and tells you it did.

Along the top of the window are the indicators. The ship labels them short and the flat board labels them long; they are the same three lights.

| On the ship | On the board | Means |
|---|---|---|
| **link** | **Screen link** | This screen is receiving the live feed. If it goes dark, this browser lost the connection — the station is probably fine, reload the page. |
| **assistant** | **AI narration** | Whether the assistant is answering. Dark is a supported state, not an error. If it reads **stand-in, not a model**, something that is not a language model is answering, and the station says so before it shows you a word of it. |
| **no scenario** | **No scenario running** | Which rehearsed timeline is running, if any. |

A fourth marker appears only during an outbreak, in red, when a crew member needs isolation and the ship has no berth left. See section 8.

## 4. Looking at one crew member

Click a row, on either view. You get their four vitals, and next to each one the reason it earned the points it earned.

You also get the list of parameters that were actually **measured**. NEWS2 has seven; this box has instruments for four. A parameter nobody measured scores zero, and a zero that means “normal” and a zero that means “nobody looked” are not the same thing. The panel says which, every time, so the screen never implies more confidence than the hardware earned.

## 5. Recording what someone tells you

Under **in their own words**, type what the crew member said and press Add. If a speech model is installed you also get a **Hold to speak** button: hold it, talk, release. What you said is transcribed on this machine and stored as their words.

A reported symptom is never a measurement, so it **never changes the NEWS2 score.** It is stored as a claim, shown as a claim, and handed to the assistant marked as a claim. Somebody saying they feel terrible does not move them up the board, and somebody saying they feel fine does not move them down.

The microphone button stays hidden until a complete speech model is on this machine, because a button that fails on the first press is worse than no button. Typing works throughout, model or no model. Fetching the model is one command and it is in `README.md`.

## 6. Asking the assistant

Select a crew member, press **Ask the assistant**. It reads that person's measurements and anything they reported, and comes back with:

- **One sentence** on what the instruments recorded.
- **Up to three patterns**, most supported first. Each is a pattern, not a diagnosis, and each carries the signs behind it.
- **Where each sign came from.** Every sign names its instrument (*temperature, spo2, pulse, respiration*) or is marked as something the crew member said and no instrument recorded.
- **How much of the data the pattern accounts for** — “one measurement fits”, “several measurements fit”, “all measured parameters fit”. That is not a confidence score. A small model has no way to know how sure it is; it can tell you how much of the data a pattern covers.
- **What to ask them next.** The box measures four things and a person can tell you a hundred, so this is often the most useful part.
- **What to find out next.** Observations and measurements, never treatments.

When the four measured parameters support nothing, it is allowed to say so and return no patterns at all. A crew member whose every reading is normal is allowed to have nothing wrong with them.

An assessment is stamped with the score it was written against. If the person's vitals move after you asked, the panel tells you the answer is stale rather than quietly leaving it on screen.

The model is `qwen2.5:1.5b-instruct`, running on this machine through Ollama. It has a hard 20-second ceiling. Past that the request is abandoned and you are told so — the box never waits on it.

## 7. When the assistant is dead

Kill Ollama mid-consultation. Nothing on the fast track notices.

What changes: the **AI narration** indicator goes dark, **Ask the assistant** reports that it is unavailable, and the station says out loud that the assistant has stopped. Every other feature in this guide keeps working, including the guide on the screen — it is rendered from data the station owns, not from the model, so the thing explaining the system does not vanish at the moment the system is proving it does not need it.

This is why the two lists in section 9 are split the way they are.

## 8. Quarantine

A crew member is isolated when they show a respiratory-transmissible pattern: a fever together with either falling oxygen or raised respiration. The rule is deliberately simple, because when somebody asks why a specific person was sealed into a specific zone, the answer has to be one sentence.

There are 3 zones (A, B, C), 4 berths each, 12 in total. A zone counts as **sealed** from the moment one person is inside it — you do not wait for a quarantine bay to fill before closing the door. Capacity governs something else: a zone at capacity stops taking new arrivals, and the next patient is placed in the next zone with room.

When all 12 berths are taken, anyone else is listed as **awaiting a bed**. They stay on the register with no zone, and they are drawn in red on both views — under the quarantine panel on the flat board, and as a marker along the top of the ship. A vessel that has run out of isolation space is the single most important fact on the screen, so it is never left to be inferred from a roster that is shorter than it should be.

Isolation is released automatically when the pattern clears.

## 9. Everything it does

This is the same list the Help button shows, from the same source.

### Works with the assistant dead

**Rank the whole crew by how ill they are**  
Every crew member is scored with NEWS2, the Royal College of Physicians early warning score, from the four vitals the hardware measures. The board and the ship are both ordered by it.  
*It is always running. Nothing to ask.*

**Show you why someone scored what they scored**  
Select a crew member and each vital carries the reason it earned its points, plus the list of which parameters were actually measured rather than assumed.  
*Click a crew member, on either view.*

**Assign isolation and seal the zone behind them**  
A febrile crew member with falling oxygen or rising respiration is assigned a quarantine berth. A zone counts as sealed from the moment one person is inside it, stops taking new arrivals once it is at capacity, and anyone left over is reported as awaiting a bed rather than quietly dropped.  
*Automatic. Watch the bulkheads close on the ship view.*

**Record what a crew member tells you**  
Type it, or say it into the microphone. It is stored as their own words and passed to the assistant as something to check. It never changes the NEWS2 score, because nothing measured it.  
*Select a crew member, then the box under 'in their own words'.*

### Needs the assistant

**Offer ranked hypotheses for one crew member**  
The assistant reads that person's measurements and anything they reported, and offers possible explanations, each sign labelled with the instrument that recorded it, or marked as something the crew member said and nothing measured. It does not diagnose, it cannot change the urgency, and when the four parameters support nothing it is allowed to say so rather than invent a pattern.  
*Select a crew member and press 'ask the assistant'.*

**Suggest what to ask the patient next**  
Because the box measures four things and a person can tell you a hundred, the most useful thing a model can do here is tell you what to ask.  
*Included in every assessment.*

4 of the 6 things this box does need no model at all. That ratio is the honest shape of the product: the AI is a narrator over a system that works without it.

## 10. Everything it will never do

Not policy, not a prompt asking it nicely. Each of these is enforced somewhere it cannot be talked out of.

**Diagnose.** It offers hypotheses with the signs behind them. There is no diagnosis field anywhere in the schema it is allowed to answer in, so it cannot emit one even if asked.

**Prescribe anything.** It has no field to put a treatment in. The one array it can fill is for observations and measurements to take, and the station drops the whole array and says so if a drug, a dose or a route appears in it. There is no doctor aboard and this box is not one.

**Change how urgent someone is.** Urgency is NEWS2, computed in Python from measurements. The model is not in that path and never reads it back.

**Act on something nobody measured.** Reported symptoms reach it marked as unverified claims. It is required to name the measurement behind every claim it makes.

**Block a reading.** It runs on a slow track. If it hangs or dies, vitals, triage, quarantine and recording carry on untouched. Kill it and watch.

**Reach the network.** The model runs locally. The vessel has no contact with Earth.

## 11. What you can type

The ship view has a command box: press `/` and type. The microphone is for what a crew member tells you, and files it as their own words, so a phrase spoken into it is recorded, not run.

| Phrase | Does | Needs the assistant |
|---|---|---|
| `worst` | Select the crew member with the highest NEWS2 score. | — |
| `next` | Move to the next crew member down the triage order. | — |
| `why` | Show how the selected score was built, parameter by parameter. | — |
| `isolated` | Show who is in quarantine and which zones are sealed. | — |
| `said <words>` | Record what this crew member just told you, in their words. | — |
| `assess` | Ask the assistant for hypotheses on the selected crew member. | yes |
| `ask` | List what to ask this patient next. | yes |
| `help` | Explain what this box can and cannot do. Works with the AI dead. | — |

`said` takes the rest of the line: `said I have had a headache since this morning`.

## 12. Running a scenario

A scenario is a rehearsed timeline applied to the synthetic crew. Pick one at the top of the window and press **Run**; **Reset** returns the crew to nominal.

**Contamination outbreak** (`contamination`)  
Six of forty crew develop a respiratory infection over ninety seconds. The board re-orders itself by NEWS2 urgency, quarantine zones fill, and partway through the AI is killed to show the station keeps working without it.

**Single patient consultation** (`single-patient`)  
One crew member develops a fever while being monitored.

**Demo from a scenario, never from live sensors.** A rehearsed replay cannot embarrass you in front of a jury. Live hardware can.

## 13. When something is wrong

| What you see | What it is | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| The board is empty and says *waiting for the station* | The page loaded but the live feed has not connected | Reload. If it persists, the station is not running — start `medbox.py` again. |
| **Screen link** dark, numbers frozen | This browser lost the feed | Reload the page. The station kept running and kept recording. |
| **AI narration** dark | Ollama is not running, or not installed | Nothing breaks. If you want it back, start Ollama and the indicator comes back on its own. |
| *The assistant cannot answer* | It was asked and it failed or timed out | The reason is printed under the message. Vitals and triage are unaffected. |
| No **Hold to speak** button | No speech model on this machine | Typing works. To add it, see *Hold-to-speak* in `README.md`. |
| The 3D view is black or will not load | No working WebGL on this machine | Use the flat board at `/board`. It has the same data. |
| Nobody is being isolated during the outbreak | Isolation needs a fever **and** either falling oxygen or raised respiration | Check the individual vitals; fever alone is monitored, not isolated. |

## 14. What is on this machine, and what is not

| | |
|---|---|
| Model | `qwen2.5:1.5b-instruct`, running locally through Ollama |
| If that model is missing | `qwen2.5:0.5b-instruct` |
| Ollama version this is built against | 0.13.1 |
| Speech out | Pre-rendered clips in the repository. Nothing to install. |
| Speech in | Transcribed on this machine. Audio never leaves it. |
| Data | A local SQLite file (`data/medbox.db`). |
| Network | None is used, at any point, by any part of this. |

The browser's own speech API was deliberately not used: it ships the microphone audio to a Google endpoint, which is not something a product whose claim is *offline* can quietly do.
